title: NVIDIA L4 Earth Observation Self-Supervised Pretraining

supported: Training loss decreased substantially during the run: 84.14% from first to last and 90.31% from first to best observed loss.
The optimizer sustained about 8.15 steps per second and processed about 195.61 sampled patches per second.
704232 samples are training samples/patches, not unique satellite scenes.
The run used 66 source images and repeatedly sampled them during self-supervised training.
The run is a valid optimization/pipeline baseline and produced a checkpoint suitable for downstream validation.
methodological_findings: The first run is a narrow-corpus baseline rather than a broad Earth survey.
The mean sampling density was about 10670 training samples per source image, so repeated patch exposure dominates the samples_seen count.
Generalization remains unmeasured because no held-out scene-level validation result is published for this run.

The public Run #1 artifact does not include a per-image manifest linking all 66 source images to location, date, sensor, scene ID and quality flags, so site-level environmental conclusions are not reproducible from this publication alone.
not_supported: The run does not by itself prove scientific environmental discoveries.
The run does not establish supervised detection accuracy because ground-truth labels were not claimed.
The run does not establish water-area change, shoreline movement, river constriction, glacier change, vegetation change or environmental causation for any named location.
Generalization must be tested on held-out, provenance-complete satellite scene pairs.

comparison_to_run_2.note: Run #2 improved public corpus/provenance coverage. Loss values across the two runs are not directly comparable because their corpora differ.
